data.title: Manufacturing's share of GDP should rise to 25% by 2047: EAC-PM chairman
data.description:
India should raise the share of manufacturing in its gross domestic product (GDP) to 25 per cent by 2047 from the current 16-17 per cent to achieve its ambition of becoming a developed economy, S Mahendra Dev, chairman of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM), said on Thursday.
 
“The share of manufacturing in GDP should rise from the present 16 to 17 per cent to 25 per cent by 2047. The transformation of the manufacturing sector is important for our goals at the time of the 100th year of India's independence,” Dev said in his address at the CII Financing Summit 2026.
 
 
He said India would need to sustain high economic growth over the next two decades to reach developed-country status. Dev said the country would need average real GDP growth of around 8 per cent annually over the next 21 years to achieve high-income status by 2047. He added that India had the potential to grow at 8-9 per cent, but sustaining this would require an expansion in productive capacity and improvements in productivity.
 
On the investment front, Dev said an investment rate of around 34-35 per cent of GDP would be important to sustain growth over the next two decades. Gross fixed capital formation stood at 31.9 per cent of GDP in 2025-26. He emphasised the need for greater private sector participation, saying public investment in infrastructure could encourage private investment by improving connectivity and reducing production and transportation costs. However, public investment alone would not be sufficient to meet the country's requirements.
 
Domestic savings would remain the principal source of financing India's investment requirements, Dev said. According to revised national accounts data, gross savings stood at 34.9 per cent of GDP in 2024-25, with the household sector accounting for around 62 per cent of the total. “Since households account for nearly two-thirds of India's domestic savings, the way these savings are used has an important bearing on how investment elsewhere in the economy is financed,” he said.
 
He said foreign capital could supplement domestic savings, but the country's own savings would remain the foundation for sustaining investment over the long term.
 
Dev also called for diversifying sources of long-term finance, saying banks alone could not meet the financing requirements of India's development ambitions. “Different investments require different kinds of finance. These requirements cannot all be met through conventional bank lending,” he said, highlighting the role of insurance and pension funds, corporate bond markets and equity markets in financing long-term investments.
 
India's corporate bond market, however, remains concentrated among highly rated issuers, with around 85-90 per cent of issuances in the highest-rated securities, Dev said. Mid-sized companies and lower-rated borrowers continue to have limited access to the market.
 
On exports, he said India's combined merchandise and services exports had reached approximately $863 billion in 2025-26, and the country was expected to cross $1 trillion in exports this year. Improving competitiveness, diversifying export markets and strengthening participation in global value chains would be crucial amid rising protectionism and geopolitical uncertainty.
 
Dev also stressed the importance of structural transformation in agriculture, manufacturing and services, alongside greater use of technology and digital public infrastructure. He called for improving agricultural productivity through diversification, post-harvest activities and agro-processing, while strengthening farmer producer organisations.
 
He said states would have to play a crucial role in achieving the 2047 vision, with each state setting its own development targets. Less-developed states such as Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh would have a greater role in India's future economic and social development.
 
“Political stability, macroeconomic stability and a large domestic economy” were the three factors underpinning India's resilience, Dev said, adding that global macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty remained a key concern.

data.title: Panchayat Season 5: Prime Video announces release date, shares new poster
data.description:
Prime Video revealed the premiere date for the fifth season of Panchayat. This season, directed by Deepak Kumar Mishra and featuring actors Jitendra Kumar, Raghubir Yadav, and Neena Gupta, is set to debut on December 3. 
 
According to a press statement issued by the production team, the upcoming season “builds on the franchise's enduring cultural connect, bringing audiences back to its quirky characters, village dynamics, and signature blend of understated humour, heartfelt moments, and local politics. ”

Panchayat season 5 poster out!

Sharing an image of Banrakas, the streamers wrote, "Batate hue khed hai, Panchayat ka agla season qaid hai. (We regret to inform you that the next season of Panchayat is currently imprisoned)."
 
 
Prime Video previously released a summary for the fifth season of Panchayat. The streamer wrote, "Facing a hostile work environment under the new vengeful leadership, Abhishek prepares to move on with his MBA dreams, but first he must tie up his loose ends in Phulera." 
ALSO READ: Ramayana crosses Rs 1,500 crore worldwide, earns over 1,000 crore in India

All about Panchayat season 5

Panchayat 5 is brought to life by The Viral Fever, commonly known as TVF. This season welcomes back its cast, including Sunita Rajwar, Faizal Malik, Chandan Roy, Sanvikaa, Durgesh Kumar, and Ashok Pathak. The series is under the direction of Deepak Kumar Mishra, who, along with Chandan Kumar and Arunabh Kumar, is credited with its creation. 
 
The makers reveal that a new ruler has emerged in Phulera, sparking curiosity regarding Banrakas's intentions as the newly appointed Pradhanpati. The question remains: can he elevate Phulera to greatness, or are his assurances merely superficial? The rise to power brings about new conflicts and evolving dynamics within Phulera.

Makers on Panchayat 5

"Some stories become special because, over time, they become a part of our lives. Panchayat is one such story," stated Manish Menghani, director and head of SVOD Content Acquisition, Prime Video India. 
 
"As one of India's most successful and recognizable franchises, it is a matter of immense pride that the series is now returning for its fifth season, a milestone that reflects its remarkable journey and continued resonance with audiences," he added. 
ALSO READ: International Men's Day 2026: Date, history, theme, significance and more

TVF on Panchayat 5

Vijay Koshy, the president of The Viral Fever (TVF), expressed that the affection viewers have displayed for Phulera and its characters has reinforced their conviction that the most straightforward narratives, presented with sincerity and emotion, can create the deepest effect.
 
"With season 5, we look forward to taking this much-loved ensemble forward, as new challenges, evolving dynamics and unexpected turns bring fresh dimensions to life in the village. Panchayat is one of the only two Indian shows on OTT to have reached its fifth season, and this milestone would not have been possible without the continued support of Prime Video. We are truly grateful for our partnership and the role they have played in making this journey so special," Vijay stated.

data.title: AI errors could pose cascading risks to financial institutions: SBI chief
data.description:
Artificial intelligence (AI)-related errors could cascade across interconnected systems, creating significant governance risks for financial institutions. Therefore, clearly defined permissions, transaction limits, audit trails and human intervention mechanisms are very important as banks increasingly deploy autonomous systems, said C S Setty, Chairman, State Bank of India (SBI), on Thursday.
 
“While AI capabilities offer substantial productivity gains, they also create new governance risks,” Setty said while speaking at an event in Mumbai. “Institutions must clearly understand what an autonomous system is authorised to do. The information it may access, the decisions it may undertake and the circumstances in which human intervention becomes mandatory,” he said.
  
Against this backdrop, Setty highlighted some key responsibilities of boards, including ensuring that the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) is driven by institutional purpose rather than technological momentum. Technology, he said, should address genuine business needs, whether by improving customer experience, strengthening risk management or widening access to financial services.
 
“Adoption cannot become an end in itself. This is particularly important in a country as diverse as India,” Setty said.
 
Setty cautioned that AI must not inadvertently exclude rural borrowers, small businesses or individuals without conventional credit histories, adding that financial inclusion must remain central to the design and deployment of the technology.
 
On governance frameworks, Setty said SBI was the first bank in the banking system to adopt a responsible AI policy, setting out principles, boundaries and accountability for the use of the technology across the organisation.
 
He said bank directors needed to build the capacity to assess model risks, data governance, cybersecurity and algorithmic bias, while understanding the limitations of AI.
 
“Today every bank board is expected to undergo a cybersecurity drill every year. And while it is still a learning process, I think now we have to integrate AI learning,” he said, adding that directors needed to understand the risks associated with AI rather than necessarily learn how to implement it. 
He also referred to the Reserve Bank of India’s AI policy, which, he said, places ultimate responsibility for AI governance on the board. At the same time, AI could improve board effectiveness by highlighting emerging risks, simplifying complex information and supporting better-informed decisions, allowing directors to devote greater attention to strategy and long-term priorities.
 
Emphasising the need to retain human accountability, Setty said AI could recommend or undertake actions, but ultimate responsibility for institutional decisions must remain with the board. “If an institution cannot adequately explain why an AI-backed process denied a loan, flagged a transaction or initiated an action, it faces serious governance challenges,” he said, underlining the importance of explainability, traceability and independent validation.
 
He added that AI was most effective in situations where parameters could be defined, relevant data was available and outcomes could be assessed. However, during crises, unexpected changes in the operating environment or strategic decisions involving unfamiliar circumstances, the collective experience and independent judgement of a board remained indispensable.
 
“The pace of AI adoption must remain commensurate with an institution’s capacity to govern the technology, particularly where decisions carry significant financial, legal, ethical or reputational consequences,” he said.
 
Setty said corporate governance was under particular stress when the pace of technological change exceeded the frameworks designed to govern it. Boards must therefore ensure that innovation advances without compromising institutional integrity and public trust.
 
“AI should complement, not substitute, the judgement and oversight of boards, strengthening their ability to discharge their responsibility while leaving accountability firmly where it belongs,” he said.
 
He highlighted that the country’s largest lender had been using artificial intelligence and machine learning, particularly in fraud risk management and business operations.
 
Among its initiatives is a patented AI and machine learning model that identifies branches that are outliers from a fraud-management perspective. The model evaluates around 23,000 branches, classifying them into very high-risk, high-risk, medium-risk and low-risk categories. The assessment helps the bank prioritise branch audits, he said.
 
However, Setty said the focus was now shifting from individual AI use cases to enterprise-level adoption, where governance would become particularly important for large institutions.
 
He identified fairness, reliability, explainability, security and accountability as critical elements of AI governance. Model bias, he said, was not merely a theoretical concern for a bank such as SBI, which serves a highly diversified customer base. “Fairness and preventing model bias are extremely important from the governance point of view,” he said.

data.title: US Democrats plan 10-yr expiry for deportation orders, green card pathways
data.description:
US House Democrats will introduce legislation on Thursday that would provide relief to certain immigrants facing final orders of removal but with no criminal convictions, while creating a pathway for them to obtain lawful permanent residency, ABC News reported on Wednesday.
 
The proposed legislation, titled the Protect Our Neighbors Act, will be introduced by California Democratic Representative Lateefah Simon, according to the report.
 
Under the proposal, final orders of removal would expire 10 years after they were issued for individuals who have remained continuously in the US and have not been convicted of a crime. Currently, such orders have no expiration date.
  
The proposal has drawn criticism from former New York City Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) field director Scott Mechkowski, who confirmed the development in a post on X.
 
"Your deportation order now comes with an expiration date. That's the Bill House Democrats are introducing tomorrow. They're calling it the Protect Our Neighbors Act," he wrote.
 
Condemning the proposal, Mechkowski said, "Nobody should be rewarded with legal status for ignoring and evading our laws."
 
He outlined how the proposed provision would work.
 
"Here's how it works. A judge orders you removed. You lose your appeals. You don't leave. Stay ten years without a criminal conviction and the order goes away. Then they hand you a path to a green card," he wrote.
 
He argued that the legislation would reward individuals who failed to comply with deportation orders, while those who left the country as directed would not receive similar benefits.
 
"Think about that. The person who obeyed the judge and went home gets nothing. The one who ignored the order gets rewarded," he said.
 
Mechkowski also questioned the provision, arguing that the legislation could undermine the authority of immigration courts.
 
"These people already had their due process. A judge heard the case. It's over. This Bill says a court order means nothing if you outlast it," he wrote.
 
He further argued that delays caused by sanctuary policies could allow individuals to remain in the US long enough for their removal orders to expire.
 
What happens to final deportation orders under the proposed Bill?
 
A final order of removal is issued by an immigration judge or immigration authorities and requires a non-US citizen to leave the country. The order becomes final after administrative appeals have been exhausted or the deadline for filing an appeal has passed.
 
Although a final removal order gives ICE the legal authority to deport an individual, it does not mean deportation takes place immediately or automatically. Removal proceedings can be delayed or suspended because of deferred action, a stay of removal, ongoing litigation or other circumstances.
 
Under the proposed legislation, an immigration judge could renew an expired final order of removal if the government establishes, through "clear and convincing evidence", that there was a substantial reason for the delay in carrying out the order.
 
The reason would have to be unrelated to administrative or funding delays. The judge would also have to determine that renewing the order was in the public interest based on new evidence, according to ABC report.
 
While Mechkowski criticised the legislation, immigration expert Andrea Flores welcomed the proposal.
 
"Glad to see the Protect Our Neighbors Act, which would create an earned path to legal residency for immigrants who may be left out of the American Dream and Promise Act," she wrote on X.
 
The legislation is also co-sponsored by California Democratic Representatives John Garamendi, Zoe Lofgren and Juan Vargas.
 
Former acting ICE Director Todd Lyons told lawmakers in February that approximately 1.6 million people in the US had final orders of deportation.
 
US deportations of Indian nationals
 
The proposed legislation comes amid expanded immigration enforcement under US President Donald Trump's second administration. The Department of Homeland Security and ICE have stepped up action against individuals with final orders of removal, including deportations to third countries.
 
Even immigrants who have regularly attended mandatory immigration check-ins have faced renewed risks of detention and deportation.
 
The development also follows Trump's remarks to CBS News' 60 Minutes, in which he said he would "love to do something on immigration" with Democrats, who are set to take control of both chambers of Congress in January following their victories in the midterm elections.
 
According to India's Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), the US deported 4,840 Indian nationals between January 2025 and July 2026. More than 6,000 Indians were deported during Trump's first presidential term, between 2017 and 2021.

data.title: Yes Bank AT-1 bondholders urge RBI to prioritise investor protection
data.description:
Holders of  Yes Bank's AT-1 bonds have written to the country's central bank, urging it to prioritise investor protection after it sought a review of a Supreme Court ruling that restored these bonds last month, according to a copy of the letter reviewed by Reuters.
 
The dispute stems from Yes Bank's rescue in 2020, when authorities wrote off ₹84.15 billion worth of additional Tier-1 (AT-1) bonds, a type of security designed to absorb losses when banks run into trouble.
 
Last month, the Supreme Court ruled the write-off illegal over procedural lapses and ordered the bonds restored. However, review petitions by the bank and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) have delayed relief for investors.
 
 
Bondholders, in their letter dated November 18, said the RBI had remained "absent" in its capacity as the regulator "responsible for protecting the interests of the investing public and the integrity of the banking system".
 
Acting on behalf of the bondholders, Axis Trustee Services Limited has separately filed a contempt petition in the Supreme Court, alleging that Yes Bank and its directors have failed to comply with court directions and have not taken any steps to restore the bonds.
 
In the contempt petition, a copy of which has been reviewed by Reuters, the trustee said bondholders, including retail investors, pension funds and provident funds, had been deprived of their investments for more than six years and still had no visibility on the restoration of the bonds and payment of coupons.
 
The trustee argued that the bank could not avoid complying with the ruling while pursuing other legal remedies because the judgment remained in force.
 
The bondholders, in their letter to the central bank, said they expected the RBI to oversee implementation of the Supreme Court verdict and protect investors rather than align itself with further challenges to the ruling.
 
The RBI and Yes Bank did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

data.title: Delhi-NCR sees 25% growth in retail space leasing in Jan-Sep: JLL
data.description:
Leasing of retail spaces in shopping malls and high streets in Delhi-NCR rose 25 per cent to 2.47 million sq ft during the first nine months of this year on better demand from retailers, according to JLL.

Real estate consultant JLL India said that the gross leasing of retail space across seven major cities increased 5.6 per cent year-on-year to 9.36 million sq ft during January-September 2026 from 8.86 million sq ft in the year-ago period.

Delhi-NCR emerged as the leading market for nine-month gross leasing, accounting for a 26 per cent share, followed closely by Mumbai (25 per cent) and Bengaluru (21 per cent).

 

The consultant said that the total gross leasing in 2026 would surpass the 12.5 million sq ft recorded in 2025, supported by continued demand from both international and domestic retailers.

Commenting on the data, S K Sayal, MD & CEO of Bharti Real Estate, said, "Retail leasing in India is witnessing robust momentum, supported by strong fundamentals such as rising consumer confidence, evolving lifestyles, and the growth of experience-led formats.

In NCR, he said there is a growing preference for mixed-use marquee spaces that seamlessly blend retail, F&B, entertainment, and modern workspaces.

As per the data, the gross leasing in Mumbai rose 39 per cent to 2.31 million sq ft in the January-September period of this calendar year.

The gross leasing in Bengaluru fell 10 per cent to 2.01 million sq ft in the first nine months of this year. The demand fell 51 per cent in Hyderabad to 0.92 million sq ft.

In Chennai, the leasing increased 27 per cent to 0.57 million sq ft. The gross leasing grew 56 per cent in Kolkata to 0.75 million sq ft.

Lastly, the leasing in Pune increased 56 per cent annually to 0.33 million sq ft in the January-September 2026.

Robin Mangla, President of M3M India, said India's retail leasing activities reflect the growing strength and maturity of the country's retail real estate market.

"This momentum is being driven by evolving consumer preferences, the expansion of organised retail and the increasing demand for well-planned, experience-led retail destinations. Retail spaces are no longer limited to shopping; they are becoming vibrant social and lifestyle hubs that bring together shopping, dining and entertainment," he added.

Manish Periwal, Senior Vice President, Pioneer Urban, noted that Gurugram continues to be the first choice for brands seeking to expand in North India.

Shriram PM Monga, Co-founder of SRED Global, said, "Indian brands are expanding rapidly and account for the bulk of the space leased, while food and entertainment operators have become some of the biggest takers of space." Monga said the growth was restricted due to lack of quality supply.

"Vacancy in good malls is falling, rents in the best malls are firming up, and brands that cannot wait are moving to high streets," he added.

During the first nine months of 2026, shopping malls captured 45.9 per cent share of total gross leasing while high streets 46.3 per cent.

Among retailers, Fashion & Apparel segment took 31 per cent of retail space, followed by food & beverage 18 per cent and entertainment 15 per cent, the JLL data showed.

data.title: Sebi approves transfer of ICICI Securities' PMS biz to ICICI Prudential AMC
data.description:
Market regulator Sebi has approved the proposed transfer of portfolio management services (PMS) business of ICICI Securities to ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company.

The proposed acquisition will be carried out through a slump sale on a going-concern basis.

"We hereby inform you that the company is in receipt of an email today... from ICICI Securities intimating receipt of a letter dated November 19, 2026, from Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) approving transfer of PMS business from ICICI Securities to the company," ICICI Prudential AMC said in a stock exchange filing on Thursday.

The company's board of directors approved the acquisition of the PMS business from ICICI Securities on August 10. Subsequently, both companies entered into a business transfer agreement for the transaction.

 

The closing of the transaction was subject to receipt of requisite regulatory approvals.

ICICI Prudential AMC said that further action in this regard would be taken in discussion with ICICI Securities.

The asset management firm reported a 6.1 per cent year-on-year rise in profit after tax (PAT) at Rs 889 crore for the September quarter of FY27 compared to ₹838 crore a year earlier, driven by higher revenue from operations.

Revenue from operations increased 16.3 per cent to ₹1,674 crore in the July-September quarter of FY27 compared to ₹1,439 crore in the year-ago period.

data.title: Trump, Xi and Putin hold first ever trilateral talks amid global tensions
data.description:
President Donald Trump met for more than an hour on Thursday with China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin, a moment that could mark a pivot in world history - or become a quickly forgotten photo op.

Trump has promoted this first-ever three-way meeting with Xi and Putin - two of America's leading rivals - as a chance to hash out rules for controlling nuclear arms and to start resolving the wars in Ukraine and Iran. Experts have kept expectations low for major breakthroughs.

"We are really making history," Trump said. "The United States, Russia and China are uniquely positioned to discuss how to reduce the number of nuclear weapons on Earth and also to lessen the risk of those weapons being used." "We will be having discussions on the theme of promoting world peace," Xi said at the start of the trilateral meeting. State broadcaster CCTV said Xi told his counterparts that he thinks nuclear weapons should be prohibited and destroyed, and called for the building of a nuclear-weapon-free world.

 

Putin harkened back to Russia, China and America's shared history as "victors in World War II," saying that "we hold joint responsibility for maintaining international peace." The last nuclear arms pact between Russia and the United States, known as New START, expired in February, and Trump has said he wants "a new, improved and modernized" deal that includes China. But China has less motivation to accept limits given that its arsenal of more than 600 warheads is far smaller than the more than 5,000 warheads believed to be in each of the US and Russian stockpiles.

"Once you have the nuclear weapons, it's very hard not to have them," Trump said. "So it's not an easy thing to do, give them up." Daryl Kimball, executive director of the Arms Control Association, said Trump's showmanship could at best start a process that would eventually lead to a sustained set of talks for reducing nuclear arsenals.

"We need more than diplomatic theater and photo opportunities between Xi, Putin and Trump at APEC," Kimball said. "And one meeting will not likely produce dramatic breakthroughs."

The leaders also talked about Iran and trade

Before the three-way meeting began on Thursday afternoon, the US president had a separate one-on-one meeting with Xi - their third substantial meeting this year. The US president praised their friendship and their shared interest in having oil shipped through the Strait of Hormuz, which has become a key site of attacks in the Iran war. Trump suggested he would push Xi to buy more agricultural products from America.

Xi said that relations between the US and China have been "generally stable and improved" during Trump's presidency. The official Chinese news agency Xinhua reported that Xi discussed Taiwan with Trump and said the two countries needed to improve communication on economic and trade issues.

Trump also added a separate sit-down with Putin to his Thursday schedule, marking the first time the leaders have held talks since their discussions in Alaska last year that failed to broker a deal to ease Russia's war in Ukraine.

"Wonderful things can come out of this - or at least start," Trump said after joining Putin for the one-on-one meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Summit, calling Putin "my friend." "We've had a great relationship for many years," Trump said after shaking hands with Putin. Their meeting lasted roughly 40 minutes.

Trump has frequently boasted of his rapport with Putin, even as relations between the US and Ukraine appear to have cratered recently. Trump rejected new Russia sanctions, while Kyiv was undermined by disruptions in satellite support for its drones during the war.

The US president added another agenda item to the trilateral meeting. He said at its opening that the trio would talk about ways to "protect our nation's sovereignty from rogue globalist organizations such as the International Criminal Court."

Trump boasts about his relationships. But the ties between Xi and Putin are stronger

The US president's ambitions recall an era of great power politics when wealthier countries felt entitled to decide the fate of seemingly lesser nations. Trump is negotiating with China and Russia without the involvement of Ukraine - or countries like Germany, France, the United Kingdom, Japan and South Korea that also have stakes in the outcome of any talks.

The US president has openly pursued a Nobel Peace Prize while also taking military actions against Venezuela and Iran.

Trump has long believed his ability to create personal connections gives him a diplomatic edge. Xi appealed to his ego Wednesday by greeting Air Force One on the airport tarmac, as the two leaders turned their handshake into a one-armed hug.

But Trump does not appear to always have the same deep relationship based on common interests that Xi and Putin share. For all the compliments the US president has showered on the two autocrats, the warmth has not always been mutually effusive.

On Wednesday at APEC, Xi greeted Putin by calling him "my old friend." The Russian leader responded by declaring Xi to be his "dear friend." China has helped economically support Russia after its 2022 invasion of Ukraine, providing Putin with a financial lifeline after the US and its allies imposed new sanctions.

By contrast, when Xi came to the White House for a state visit in September, he was far more restrained with Trump, saying they had built a "personal rapport and stayed in touch." Trump and Xi plan to meet a total of four times this year, with their final time together coming in December at the G20 summit being held at the Trump National Doral Golf Club in Florida.

Still, there were signs of friction Thursday in the US-China relationship despite Trump's praise of Xi.

Chinese officials blocked a Bloomberg reporter, Annmarie Hordern, from the trilateral meeting after she asked a question at the earlier Trump-Xi session.

Chinese television showed a video of Trump appearing drowsy, while the White House posted a clip of Trump helping Xi up an escalator.

Conflicts on AI also hang over the meetings

While Trump views his relationship with China as a positive, it has not necessarily resulted in meaningful changes between the world's two largest economies. China continues to run large trade surpluses with the rest of the world, while the US has almost equally large trade deficits.

And the race between the US and China to master artificial intelligence has grown tense over the past two weeks. Trump's ally Jensen Huang resigned last week as the CEO of Nvidia after confessing to an extramarital affair with a woman, Alice Huang, whose company helped to give China access to the company's advanced computer chips used to develop AI models. Beijing has denied that Alice Huang was a Chinese government agent.

Trump held off on imposing tougher restrictions on China's ability to access the chips, suggesting he did not want to insult China and aggravate relations.

US officials have said that China had not fully honoured its commitments made last year in a Trump-Xi meeting to buy more US agricultural products and loosen restrictions on the sale of rare earth minerals needed for electronics.

The trade truce between the US and China reached last year after duelling tariff hikes is set to expire by Jan. 10 next year.

Meanwhile, both China and Russia have used trade to support Iran, even during the US war on that country, which has pushed up energy prices and reduced global economic growth.
